purpose: Direct early-UE4 style study applied to the user's actual screenshot and exact arrangement
reference_mode: last three images: 2014 UMG screenshot, 2014 Persona screenshot, user's current Quader app
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup / style-transfer.

TASK: Restyle the user's ACTUAL QUADER APP SCREENSHOT (Image 3) using the visual language of the two REAL EARLY UNREAL ENGINE 4 screenshots (Images 1 and 2). Produce one complete widescreen desktop-app mockup. The user has rejected flat, overly tidy, homogenized, modern mockups. The references' actual early-UE4 character is essential.

REFERENCE ROLES:
Image 1: real August 2014 UE4 UMG editor. STYLE ONLY. Ignore the black exterior padding, central game menu, timeline, branding and all functionality. Study its shaped title rail, lighter gray toolbar deck, tabbed fitted dock chrome, recessed control wells and short gradients.
Image 2: real August 2014 UE4 Persona editor. STYLE ONLY. Ignore black exterior padding, the character scene and animation functions. Study the pictorial shaded icons, varied control sizes, beveled tab silhouettes, mid-gray structural framing, dark recesses and localized amber accents.
Image 3: THE USER'S CURRENT QUADER APP. This is the authoritative EDIT TARGET for all arrangement and content. Preserve this exact working layout and this exact scene. It supersedes every earlier Quader mockup. Do not use any previous generated image as style or arrangement guidance.

LOCK THE USER'S ARRANGEMENT:
- Very compact title/menu strip at top, then two existing tool strips. Preserve all actual menu labels, Edit Mode, mesh selection symbols, Grid 32, Angle 15°, modeling icons and viewport controls.
- LEFT column about 14% of width: Outliner on top, Inspector immediately below. Inspector stays LEFT, not right.
- CENTER about 65% of width: one huge perspective viewport reaching down to the status bar. Preserve the precise scene and camera: black perspective grid, checker-textured curved wall fixtures toward the upper right, checker geometry cropped at the lower right, selected bent polygonal piece near the lower-center with brown side faces, concrete front faces, cyan edges and the small yellow dimension cage. No replacement hallway, no new stairs or pillars.
- RIGHT column about 21% of width: Face Texture panel. The large concrete texture canvas with its white quadrilateral/cyan control points occupies the upper portion. Beneath are Texture Settings and Edit Texture controls, then the compact material thumbnail browser and search field at the bottom.
- NO bottom-spanning Asset Browser. NO far-left vertical modeling-tool rail. NO new feature panes.
- Preserve exact relative panel sizes, locations, user scene content, visible fields, selection, controls and existing state. Changes are to visual design only.

ACTUAL EARLY-UE4 LOOK TO APPLY:
A collection of substantial specialized native editor tools fitted together. Deliberately VARIED visual rhythm: beveled tab heads, short raised buttons, shallow scooped numeric fields, compact checkbox rows, narrow comboboxes, larger shaded modeling pictograms, thinner utility glyphs and dense thumbnail wells. The forms should follow their purpose, not an identical flat rectangle system.
RICH MULTI-VALUE CHARCOAL PALETTE: medium-gray structural decks around #555555, warm charcoal working panels around #3C3C3C, dark inset content around #262626, almost-black seams. This is still a DARK THEME: no white/cream page backgrounds and no giant bright areas. Use a materially wider range of gray values than the rejected near-black/black mockups.
FUNCTIONAL RELIEF: clear but shallow bevels, top-edge highlights, inset shadow lines, visibly sculpted pressed/unpressed states, short directional gradients and fitted double-edge viewport framing. The dock title is a small SHAPED TAB connected to the frame with unused rail beside it, not a uniform full-width modern heading ribbon. Compact segmented/overlapping tab silhouettes may have the gentle sloped shoulders seen in the reference. Preserve the label and tool positions.
ILLUSTRATED ICONS: real little dimensional objects with recognizable silhouettes, soft local shading, small highlights, and blue-gray/ochre/steel color. Keep Quader's actual modeling tool meanings and general symbols. Do not replace everything with generic cubes or fashionable line icons. Allow unequal icon shapes and natural grouping without making every control a matching square tile.
COMPACT NATIVE TYPOGRAPHY: ordinary small Windows UI font with modest semibold headings; no giant text, artificial wide tracking, poster type or uniformly bold labels. Preserve actual information density, thin conventional separators and irregular function-driven group widths from the screenshot. Do not simplify the screen into a clean showcase.
COLOR WITH PURPOSE: retain small Quader-purple branding/check states, the orange active viewport border, cyan geometry edges, yellow dimension cage and RGB axis coloring. Introduce localized warm ochre/orange active-tab treatment inspired by early UE4, but don't flood the app with one accent hue. Numeric fields can be a lighter mid-gray with dark inset edges and legible light text; they must visibly differ from labels.
SURFACES should have that slightly old-school digital sculpting of 2014 Slate, not physical grunge. The interface should feel hands-on, substantial, individual, a little visually eclectic, and professional. The exact forms in Images 1 and 2 take priority over generic "polished product design".

INSPECTOR AND FACE TEXTURE DETAILS:
Keep Inspector General / Visibility / Transform / Material / Export / Lighting / Viewport / Physics in their current left-column arrangement. Keep Location, Rotation and Scale with STACKED X/Y/Z component rows. Keep right-side UV Scale U/V paired horizontally, Shift U/V paired horizontally and Rotation below, followed by Edit Texture and materials. Do not reflow these into a new arrangement. Show enough individual widget shapes and natural density to resemble real working software.

OUTPUT:
One full-window 2560x1392-proportioned image, crisp and detailed, no device, no webpage, no exterior padding, no design-board annotation. Preserve the working screenshot content and change the chrome decisively toward the real early UE4 references.
AVOID: flat blocks, SaaS cards, "perfect" matching control grids, sleek 2026 minimalism, uniformly squared buttons, floating rounded cards, neon purple, giant branding, sci-fi HUDs, chrome plating, decorative rivets, rough paper, punk/grunge, scratches, band/poster motifs, gothic type. Do not add game menu, timeline, Play button or any Unreal feature.
